description: Change semantics for every module field cluster:vm owns — the reference manifest for ADR-020 D3/D4.
_note: Every class below is a STATEMENT OF EXISTING BEHAVIOUR, read off update-service.sh as it stood before ADR-020: what it applies via the single batched `qm set`, what it grows, what it migrates, what it warns about and what it refuses. Nothing here changes what happens today; P3 makes update-service.sh read this file instead of hardcoding the same knowledge in an imperative drift loop.

vmname.changeNote: Proxmox spells the guest name 'name'. Only reconciled when the guest reports one.

vmtag.changeNote: Proxmox stores tags lowercased, de-duplicated and ';'-joined; module JSON may use mixed case and commas. The 'tags' normalizer is that canonicalisation, moved from update-service.sh's normalize_tags into the one differ. The schema default 'TAPPaaS' is DESIRED state, not just a create-time seed (ADR-020 D9): an undeclared vmtag means the guest should carry exactly 'TAPPaaS', which is also what both create paths apply, so config and guest agree from install without an adoption step. qm set --tags REPLACES the list, so a tag added in the Proxmox UI is drift and the converge writes it back — intended: config is authoritative.

cputype.description: CPU type emulation for the VM
cputype.note: Use 'host' for best performance, or a specific CPU model for migration compatibility
cputype.changeNote: Proxmox spells it 'cpu'. The undeclared default resolves to 'host' — from module-fields.json, via the one resolver, NOT from a cfg() ladder in this service (#550).

bridge0.changeNote: A bridge change moves the guest to a different L2 segment, so it must re-DHCP — hence the reboot.

zone0.changeNote: The zone resolves to net0's VLAN tag; a new tag is a new subnet, so the guest must renew DHCP and re-register DNS.

mac0.changeNote: A new MAC is a NEW IDENTITY on the wire: the guest takes a fresh DHCP lease, very likely a different address, and its DNS record must follow — exactly the reboot → wait-for-lease → re-register chain net0 already declares. Classed in-place until ADR-020 P6, inherited from a comment that grouped 'trunk- or MAC-only' changes as live; the two are not alike, because trunks is a BRIDGE-side allow-list the guest never sees while the MAC is the guest's own NIC. #194 already established that a netN property needing device re-creation (queues) is a disruptive hot-replug, and the MAC takes the same path. When the module pins no mac0 the field has no desired value at all and the LIVE MAC is carried across, which is why the manager assembles the finished netopts — so this only bites a module that deliberately re-MACs a guest.

trunks0.changeNote: A trunk-only change applies live on the bridge — no reboot.

bridge1.description: Proxmox bridge for the VM's second network interface (net1). The sentinel 'NONE' — which is also what an absent bridge1 resolves to — means the VM has only one NIC.
bridge1.note: cluster:vm only — a container has ONE NIC in TAPPaaS: neither Create-TAPPaaS-LXC.sh nor cluster:lxc's install/update service mentions net1, so the cluster:lxc claim these fields used to carry (bridge1/mac1/zone1/trunks1) was ownership that did not exist, removed in ADR-020 P5. Only used if a second network interface is needed. The default was 'lan' until ADR-020 P1, which contradicted both acting paths — Create-TAPPaaS-VM.sh and cluster:vm/update-service.sh have always read it as 'NONE' — and made the drift report claim a desired second NIC that nothing would ever create. Declaring a bridge1 on a VM that has none ADDS the NIC; removing it (back to the 'NONE' default) DELETES the live net1, which reboots the guest.
bridge1.changeNote: Also the ADD/REMOVE switch for the second NIC. Its module-fields.json default is the sentinel 'NONE', so an undeclared bridge1 resolves to 'no second NIC' — the same reading Create-TAPPaaS-VM.sh and update-service.sh have always had. 'NONE' with a live net1 means the NIC is removed, which likewise reboots.

zone1.description: Security zone for net1. Must exist in zones.json.
zone1.note: Only used if bridge1 is defined. Hyphens are NOT allowed — use underscores (#237).

mac1.description: MAC address for the net1 network port
mac1.changeNote: As mac0: a new MAC means a new lease and a new DNS record, so it earns net1's reboot chain. Unpinned, the live MAC is preserved and nothing drifts.

trunks1.description: Semicolon-separated list of additional zone names to trunk on net1. Same format as trunks0.
trunks1.note: Only used if bridge1 is defined. Zone names must exist in zones.json, camelCase only [a-zA-Z0-9].

diskSize.changeNote: A grow goes through resize-disk.sh. The direction is only knowable against the live size, so a SHRINK is refused at apply time (hook exit 20), not by the static pre-gate. The schema default 8G is DESIRED state (ADR-020 D9): it is also what both create paths build with, so an undeclared guest is in sync from install. When the guest is later grown outside the config path — check-disk-threshold.sh, resize-disk.sh by hand, qm resize — config falls BEHIND actual, which reads as a shrink and would be refused on every converge forever. That case is now ADOPTED instead: the converge writes the observed size into config, touching nothing on the cluster. Excluding undeclared modules from the comparison, as v0.5 did, never helped here: a DECLARED module — which is all of them — got the permanent refusal anyway.

node.changeNote: The ADR-019 bridge. The hook routes HA-vs-non-HA internally: a module that dependsOn cluster:ha has its node drift handled by the HA rule (re-point), a plain module by qm migrate. Live-OK decides whether the migrate needs downtime, so this refuses (exit 10) rather than migrating offline without --force. module-fields.json gives node NO default, so a module that declares none has no desired placement and is left where it runs. update-service.sh instead defaulted it to the FIRST site node, which would silently migrate an undeclared guest back to node 0 after any failover or manual move — a latent hazard that only stayed invisible because the estate's undeclared guests happen to sit on node 0. Expressing no placement is not the same as asking for node 0.

storage.changeNote: A storage change means moving the disk, and update-service.sh has always WARNED rather than acting, because an implicit qm move-disk is a long, IO-heavy operation an operator must schedule. Not pre-gated: writing the intended storage into config and reporting the gap is useful, so only the apply refuses. The schema default 'tanka1' is DESIRED state (ADR-020 D9) — it is what both create paths build on, so an undeclared guest is in sync from install. Nothing in TAPPaaS ever moves a disk, so this can only diverge when an operator runs qm move-disk by hand, and reporting exactly that is what the manual class is for; Excluding undeclared modules from the comparison suppressed exactly that report, which is the opposite of what manual means.

values.seabios: Legacy BIOS (for older OSes or special cases)

bios.changeNote: Firmware is chosen when the guest is created; changing it on a live VM is refused (main's update-service made it the script's only FATAL). Pre-gated, so config is never left claiming a firmware the guest does not have. Proxmox OMITS the bios: line for seabios, so an absent value decodes to seabios rather than unknown. The schema default 'ovmf' is DESIRED state (ADR-020 D9) and is what Create-TAPPaaS-VM.sh builds with, so a guest TAPPaaS created always matches it. The residual risk is a guest built ELSEWHERE and adopted while declaring nothing — on seabios it would report recreate drift that fails the converge and can never be resolved in place. install-service.sh therefore records the observed firmware into config at install, which closes that case at the only moment it can be closed.

ostype.description: Proxmox guest OS profile. Controls QEMU clock, ACPI, and balloon-driver behaviour — it does NOT install the OS. The letter in 'l26' is a lowercase L (Linux), not the digit 1.
ostype.note: Pick the value that matches your guest OS. Wrong ostype causes clock drift or incorrect power-management behaviour but does not prevent the VM from booting.

values.l26: Linux kernel 2.6 and later — NixOS, Debian, Ubuntu, and any modern Linux distro. Enables KVM paravirtual clock, assumes UTC hardware clock. USE THIS for all TAPPaaS NixOS and Debian/Ubuntu VMs.
values.win11: Windows 11 / Windows Server 2022 / Windows Server 2025. Enables Windows-specific ACPI, local-time hardware clock, Hyper-V enlightenments, and TPM 2.0 support. USE THIS for all Windows Server 2025 VMs.
values.win10: Windows 10 / Windows Server 2016 / Windows Server 2019. Same Windows treatment as win11 but with an earlier ACPI profile.
values.win2k25: Explicit alias for Windows Server 2025. Equivalent to win11 in Proxmox — win11 is preferred.
values.win2k22: Explicit alias for Windows Server 2022. Equivalent to win11 in Proxmox — win11 is preferred.
values.win2k19: Explicit alias for Windows Server 2019. Equivalent to win10 in Proxmox — win10 is preferred.
values.other: Generic / unknown OS — minimal hypervisor optimisation.

ostype.changeNote: A creation-time hint that selects emulated hardware defaults; never reconciled on a live guest.

autoInstall.description: Whether this template can be built fully automatically without operator input. Used by cluster:vm/install-service.sh when a required template is missing — if true, the template is auto-built before the clone proceeds; if false, the operator must build it manually first.

values.true: Fully unattended build — no console interaction required (e.g. tappaas-winserver with autounattend.xml)
values.false: Requires manual installation — operator must run install-module.sh and complete the setup (e.g. tappaas-nixos graphical installer)

autoInstall.changeNote: Drives the unattended install at creation. Meaningless afterwards.

sshAccess.description: Whether TAPPaaS can manage this guest over SSH. Set false for sealed appliance images that expose no login shell (e.g. Home Assistant OS). When false, cluster:vm test-service skips its SSH-based health checks (connectivity, disk, memory) and relies on the module's own test.sh for app-level health — so a working appliance is not falsely reported as failing (which would otherwise abort updates).

values.true: TAPPaaS manages the guest over SSH (NixOS VMs, OPNsense as root)
values.false: Unmanaged appliance — no SSH; skip SSH-based cluster:vm tests

sshAccess.changeNote: Seeds the cloud-init SSH configuration at creation.

vmid.changeNote: The guest's identity. Changing it IS a different guest — delete + reinstall.

os.description: Operating system family of the VM. Drives OS-specific cloud-init bootstrapping (e.g. attaching the Debian vendor-data snippet that pre-installs qemu-guest-agent).
os.default: <auto-detected from image filename: debian-*, ubuntu-*, *nixos* -> matching value; else unknown>

values.debian: Debian-family cloud image (apt). Receives the tappaas-debian vendor-data snippet.
values.ubuntu: Ubuntu-family cloud image (apt). Receives the tappaas-debian vendor-data snippet.
values.nixos: NixOS template VM. No vendor-data snippet.
values.windows: Windows Server clone VM. Create-TAPPaaS-VM.sh builds and attaches a per-VM OOBE answer ISO. No cloud-init.
values.unknown: OS family is unknown. No vendor-data snippet.

os.note: Optional. If omitted, Create-TAPPaaS-VM.sh falls back to sniffing the 'image' filename. Set explicitly to override the sniff.
os.changeNote: Auto-detected from the image at install and never changed in place. Reported from the QEMU guest agent (get-osinfo), whose distro id the reporter maps into this schema's vocabulary — Windows spells itself 'mswindows'. The agent only answers for a RUNNING guest with the agent installed; otherwise the reporter omits the key and the field records as not-reported rather than drifting against an empty actual.

imageType.changeNote: clone vs. download decides how the guest was built; it cannot be re-decided in place.

imageLocation.description: URL or local path where the image file is located. For images already on the Proxmox node use the local directory path (e.g. '/var/lib/vz/template/iso/'). For remote images use an https:// URL.
imageLocation.note: For apt, if present, names an additional package repository to add

cloudInit.description: Whether the VM supports cloud-init for initial configuration

values.true: VM supports cloud-init (SSH keys, hostname, etc.)

cloudInit.changeNote: How the guest was provisioned; not re-decidable in place. Observed as the presence of the '<storage>:vm-<vmid>-cloudinit' drive, which is always readable from qm config, so this is reported for every guest — 'false' means the guest genuinely has no cloud-init drive.

net0.changeNote: The primary NIC: one qm value 'virtio=<mac>,bridge=<b>,tag=<vlan>[,trunks=…][,queues=…]' assembled from four declared fields. The MANAGER builds the finished string because it must preserve two LIVE values the config never carries — the MAC when the module pins none, and queues, which must never change on a running NIC (#194). in-place-reboot is the CEILING: the runner escalates only when bridge0 or zone0 actually drifted; a MAC- or trunk-only change stays in-place, exactly as today.

net1.changeNote: The optional second NIC. Adding it, or changing its bridge/tag, reboots; a trunk- or MAC-only change applies live. Removing it (bridge1 gone from config while the guest still has net1) is a `qm set --delete net1` and also reboots.
